name: Arnold Beckman
milestone_by_age_26: Material breakthrough arrived after age 26: invented the commercially successful electronic pH meter (acidimeter) in 1934 at age 34 and founded National Technical Laboratories (later Beckman Instruments) in 1935 at age 35. Earlier achievements include a bachelor's (1922, age 22) and master's (1923, age 23) from the University of Illinois and a Caltech PhD (1928, age 28), but the defining invention and company founding were mid-30s.
early_history_summary: Born in Cullom, Illinois, to a blacksmith father; discovered chemistry via an attic textbook at age 9 and ran experiments in a toolshed lab. Graduated high-school valedictorian, worked as a wartime chemist and U.S. Marine, earned B.S. (1922) and M.S. (1923) at Illinois, worked at Western Electric/Bell Labs on vacuum tubes, then completed a Caltech Ph.D. in photochemistry (1928) and joined the Caltech faculty.
family_context_summary: Youngest son of George Beckman, a blacksmith in rural Cullom, Illinois; mother Elizabeth died of diabetes when he was about 12. Father later worked as a traveling salesman for blacksmithing tools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a blacksmith who encouraged Arnold's scientific tinkering by converting a toolshed into a lab; not an academic or industrial chemistry lineage.
evidence_summary: Biographies from Wikipedia, Science History Institute, Lemelson-MIT, and ACS consistently date the pH-meter invention to 1934 and company founding to 1935 (ages 34–35). Degrees through age 23 and PhD at 28 do not substitute for the commercial scientific-instrument breakthrough that defines his trajectory.

name: Serafina Brocious
milestone_by_age_26: At age 17 (2005), as high-school student Cody Brocious, co-created PyMusique with Jon Lech Johansen, a Linux client for the iTunes Music Store that purchased songs without FairPlay DRM—covered nationally by Forbes and NBC News.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania (also associated with Waukegan, Illinois in later bios). As a Linux-using 11th grader, reverse-engineered iTunes purchase flows with collaborators including DeCSS author Jon Lech Johansen. Later reverse-engineered Emotiv EPOC EEG protocol (2010), published the Hardware Hacker Manifesto, and at Black Hat 2012 demonstrated Onity hotel lock vulnerabilities affecting millions of rooms.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond geographic ties to Chambersburg, PA and Waukegan, IL.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen reverse engineering, demoscene/open source, PyMusique, Black Hat Onity, peer collab with Johansen
evidence_summary: Forbes and NBC (March 2005) independently report Brocious as a 17-year-old 11th grader who co-built PyMusique. Wikipedia and later coverage document continued security research (Emokit 2010; Onity hotel locks at Black Hat 2012). Wired describes Brocious as a 24-year-old around the 2012 lock disclosure, consistent with birth around 1988. Family background is sparse; advantage stack is self-taught technical depth plus open-source/online distribution rather than institutional pedigree.
starting_point: Not documented in detail; grew up in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania, active as a Linux-oriented high-school programmer by the mid-2000s.
current_position: American software engineer and security researcher known for PyMusique and the 2012 Onity hotel-lock disclosure; has worked at firms including Optiv (per Wikipedia).

trajectory.event: Co-created PyMusique, a Linux iTunes Music Store client that purchased songs without FairPlay DRM, drawing national press as a 17-year-old.
Co-founded Falling Leaf Systems to commercialize the Alky Project for running Windows games on Linux/Mac.
Reverse-engineered the Emotiv EPOC EEG headset protocol and published the AES key and Hardware Hacker Manifesto.
Presented Onity HT hotel lock vulnerabilities at Black Hat, showing millions of hotel rooms could be opened with cheap hardware.
Onity lock findings continued to drive industry response and were linked in reporting to real-world hotel burglaries exploiting the flaw.

name: Gregory Abowd

Held research posts at York and Carnegie Mellon before joining Georgia Tech's faculty in 1994, where he became a leading ubiquitous-computing researcher.
family_context_summary: Raised in Farmington Hills, a Detroit suburb; family financial and occupational details not documented in reviewed sources.

The Rhodes/Oxford path by the early twenties is a specific, multi-source-supported material academic milestone before 26; major ubicomp systems (Cyberguide, Classroom 2000, Aware Home) and ACM Fellow recognition came later in his career.
starting_point: Born and raised in Farmington Hills, Michigan; family class/occupation not detailed in reviewed sources.
current_position: Dean of the College of Engineering and Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Northeastern University (appointed 2021); previously longtime Georgia Tech professor of interactive computing.

trajectory.event: Graduated summa cum laude in honors mathematics from Notre Dame and was selected as a Rhodes Scholar.
Completed M.Sc. in Computation at the University of Oxford.

name: Caroline Ellison
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Alameda Research as a trader in March 2018 at age 23 after Jane Street; by October 2021 (still age 26, born November 1994) became co-CEO of Alameda Research, the major crypto trading firm affiliated with FTX.
early_history_summary: Born November 1994 in Boston to MIT economists Glenn Ellison and Sara Fisher Ellison; raised in Cambridge/Newton, Massachusetts with early exposure to economics and competitive math (AMC honors, Math League captain, International Linguistics Olympiad honorable mention). Graduated Stanford math in 2016 (age ~21), interned and then worked full-time at Jane Street, then joined Alameda in 2018 and rose to co-CEO (2021) and sole CEO (2022).
family_context_summary: Eldest of three daughters of Glenn Ellison and Sara Fisher Ellison, both MIT economists; raised Catholic in Cambridge and Newton, MA; parents coached math teams and exposed children to Bayesian statistics early.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents are MIT economics professors; father coached her middle-school math team; strong quantitative/academic apprenticeship environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT economist parents, Stanford math, Jane Street, Putnam, effective altruism network, crypto trading wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Boston Globe, WSJ, and Forbes document November 1994 birth, Stanford 2016, Jane Street path, Alameda join in 2018 (age 23), and co-CEO elevation in October 2021 (age 26). Family domain advantage (two MIT economist parents) and elite math pipeline are multi-source supported. Later pleaded guilty to fraud related to FTX/Alameda collapse, was sentenced to two years, and was released after ~14 months in January 2026.
starting_point: Born November 1994 in Boston to MIT economists Glenn and Sara Fisher Ellison; raised in Cambridge and Newton, Massachusetts with intense early math/economics exposure.
current_position: Former Alameda Research CEO; pleaded guilty to fraud in the FTX collapse, sentenced to two years (2024), released from federal custody in January 2026 after serving about 14 months.

trajectory.event: Graduated Stanford with a B.S. in mathematics and joined Jane Street Capital full-time as an equities trader.
Joined Alameda Research as a cryptocurrency trader after being recruited by Sam Bankman-Fried.
Named co-CEO of Alameda Research with Sam Trabucco as Bankman-Fried stepped back from day-to-day trading leadership.
Became sole Alameda CEO; firm and FTX collapsed in November amid revelations of customer-fund misuse; pleaded guilty to multiple fraud counts in December.
Testified as a key prosecution witness in the criminal trial of Sam Bankman-Fried.
Sentenced to two years in prison and ordered to forfeit $11 billion; reported to federal prison in Connecticut.
Released from federal custody after serving approximately 14 months.
